subject: SIG: infrastructure evidence for VPC peering and private endpoint IPs
messages:
From: James Reynolds <jreynolds@corpnet.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: CorpNet Security Team <security@corpnet.io>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: network evidence needed for VPC peering / private endpoint

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As part of our SIG review we need a concise packet of evidence for the network section (VPC peering, private endpoints, and IP allowlists). Can you provide the following by end of week?

- VPC peering request/confirmation (manifest or ticket ID)
- List of egress IP ranges used by Redwood for the hosted control plane and inference endpoints
- DNS export for the private endpoint(s) (A/CNAME records and TTLs)
- A short traceroute or connectivity check from our VPC to the private endpoint to show routing

If any items are controlled by your infra team and will come from an engineer, please loop them in.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a 15m call if helpful.

Best,
James
James Reynolds
Senior InfoSec Manager, CorpNet Health
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: James Reynolds <jreynolds@corpnet.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: network evidence needed for VPC peering / private endpoint

Hi James —

Thanks for the clear list. We're assembling a single packet and will hand off the network artifacts from infra. Attaching initial files: redwood_vpc_peering_manifest.pdf and egress_ip_ranges.csv.

Quick clarifications so we provide exactly what you need:
- Do you need WHOIS/ASN documentation for the egress ranges, or is a signed CSV sufficient?
- For the private endpoint DNS export: should we include internal-only CNAME chains (private hosted zone entries) or only the public-facing records that your routing will observe?

I'll ask Karthik to run a traceroute and a DNS export and add his notes. Expect a follow-up email with the traceroute_logs.txt and private_endpoint_dns_export.csv by tomorrow afternoon.

Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: James Reynolds <jreynolds@corpnet.io>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: network evidence needed for VPC peering / private endpoint

Hi James — looping in with the infra artifacts you requested. Summary below and attached files.

What I attached:
- private_endpoint_dns_export.csv — exported from our private hosted zone (includes internal CNAME chains and final A records)
- traceroute_logs.txt — traceroute from a test instance in us-west-2 to the private endpoint; shows next-hop through our transit gateway and private link route table entries

Short notes:
- Peering manifest: redwood_vpc_peering_manifest.pdf (includes ticket ID: PEER-4821, timestamps, and security contact)
- Egress IPs: egress_ip_ranges.csv lists static ranges we announce for control-plane egress; these are the stable ranges we ask customers to allowlist. Where ephemeral NAT is used we called it out in the CSV notes column.
- DNS: We included internal TTLs and the private-zone mapping. Our private endpoint resolves only inside the peered VPC; we do not publish those A records to public DNS.

If you need BGP session dumps or ASN statements for routing proofs, let me know and I can pull them.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: James Reynolds <jreynolds@corpnet.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: network evidence needed for VPC peering / private endpoint

Irene/Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts, this is exactly what our security reviewers needed. A couple quick follow-ups before we close the SIG item:

1) For the egress ranges CSV: can you add a one-line attest statement (signed by your network lead) confirming these are the ranges you expect to use for control-plane traffic for the next 90 days? A PDF with the lead's name and date is fine.
2) For the private endpoint DNS: can you export a screenshot of the hosted zone entries in the console (or a CSV with headers visible) so our auditors can match fields to the DNS export?

If you can send both by early next week we'll mark this as resolved on our end. Appreciate it.

Best,
James
